memory_update.text: AVGO, ANET, NVDA, MRVL, and COHR form a high-priority US-listed direct-exposure set for AI networking, optics, and cluster fabric.

The node should be split in later layers into: Ethernet switch ASICs/fabric routers, switch systems/EOS software, NVIDIA closed/full-stack fabrics, optical DSP/coherent DCI, CPO, pluggable optics/transceivers, lasers/components, and manufacturing/EMS.

Additional US-listed names to evaluate in a later pass include CIEN, LITE, FN, AAOI, CSCO, JNPR, SMTC, NOK, and possibly private/non-US leaders such as InnoLight, Eoptolink, Innolux/ODM suppliers, and Taiwan/China/Japan optical component suppliers.
This pass did not assess valuation, revenue concentration, cyclicality, or whether AI-related demand is already priced in; those require a market-pricing and falsification layer.
AVGO is a high-confidence direct candidate for AI cluster fabric due to official AI revenue disclosure and Tomahawk/Jericho Ethernet switch ASIC positioning.
ANET is a high-confidence systems/software candidate for Ethernet AI fabrics; later layers should separate durable AI back-end deployments from general cloud refresh and campus/routing growth.
MRVL is a high-confidence connectivity semiconductor candidate across optical DSPs, coherent DSPs, SerDes, and custom silicon; key open question is revenue mix and design-win durability.
LITE is a direct optics/photonic-component candidate, strengthened by NVIDIA’s 2026 strategic agreement; key risks are customer concentration, capacity execution, and cyclical telecom/datacom mix.
FN is a second-order optical manufacturing/packaging candidate; include because manufacturing yield and precision optical assembly may become hidden bottlenecks behind transceiver OEMs.

Not included due to 5-candidate cap but should be evaluated in later passes: COHR for optical transceivers/lasers/materials and NVIDIA partnership; CIEN for DCI/coherent optics and WaveLogic; CSCO/HPE/JNPR/NOK for networking systems; AAOI for smaller optical-module exposure; CIEN/COHR/LITE/FN comparisons need AI revenue purity checks.

Add CRDO as a high-priority AI fabric candidate focused on active electrical cables, SerDes/DSP, and optical/electrical connectivity; key risk is customer concentration and hyperscaler deployment timing.
Add ALAB as a high-priority rack-scale AI connectivity candidate spanning PCIe/CXL/Ethernet/NVLink/UALink plus COSMOS observability; verify protocol-specific revenue and platform attach rates.
Add APH as a diversified but potentially underappreciated physical interconnect supplier for AI datacenter high-speed, power, and fiber-optic connectivity.
Add KEYS as an adjacent chokepoint supplier for AI fabric validation, 800G/1.6T Ethernet emulation, 224G SerDes, and optical/electrical test equipment.
Add SMTC as an optical-component candidate in low-power 400G/800G AI data-center optics via TIAs, laser drivers, and LPO-related analog PMD technology.

Future Layer 1B passes should map US-listed or ADR exposure in optical transceiver/module manufacturing, photonics equipment, laser sources, fiber/cable assemblies, and network observability software separately from this five-name batch.

node: AI networking, optics, and cluster fabric
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion for the AI cluster-fabric node identifies five US-listed, direct-exposure companies spanning switch ASICs and CPO, Ethernet switching systems, full-stack AI networking platforms, optical/DSP semiconductors, and optical transceiver/component manufacturing. This is not a buy/sell list; it is a research universe for later evidence, revenue-quality, customer-concentration, and market-pricing checks. Expanded US-listed universe for the AI cluster-fabric node. The strongest direct exposures are merchant/custom networking silicon, Ethernet switching systems, optical DSP/SerDes/connectivity semiconductors, photonic components/lasers, and precision optical manufacturing. This pass prioritizes suppliers whose products may become capacity or qualification chokepoints as AI clusters move from accelerator scarcity toward fabric, optics, congestion control, and observability constraints. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded the node universe toward less-obvious second-order AI fabric beneficiaries: active electrical cables, PCIe/CXL/Ethernet retimers and switches, high-speed interconnect hardware, optical analog PMDs, and validation/test equipment for 800G/1.6T fabrics. These are not buy/sell recommendations; they are research candidates for later evidence scoring, revenue durability checks, customer concentration analysis, and market-pricing review.
